# Triage: `pub` items with no consumer outside their own file

*Generated by `scripts/scan-pub-item-usage.py --triage`. Do not hand-edit.*

Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 scripts/scan-pub-item-usage.py --triage \
  --enterprise ../sbproxy-enterprise > scripts/pub-item-triage.md
```

## Verdicts

| Verdict | Meaning | Tests-only | All |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `escalated` | A finding too big to settle inside a cleanup PR. Tracked separately; see scripts/pub-item-verdicts.json for the reason. | 0 | 5 |
| `keep` | Live through a consumer this repository cannot see: the out-of-tree tree, serde/schemars, or a reason recorded in scripts/pub-item-verdicts.json. | 45 | 296 |
| `narrow` | Used inside its own file. Wrong visibility, not dead code. Narrowing to `pub(crate)` shrinks the public surface and lets `dead_code` police it from then on. | 129 | 778 |
| `wire-or-delete` | No consumer anywhere and no in-file use. Give it a production call site or remove it. | 34 | 87 |

Tests-only total: **208**. Full candidate list: **1166**.

`narrow` is the highest-leverage verdict and should be preferred over deletion
wherever it applies. It converts an item rustc cannot see into one it polices for
free, so the same item can never rot silently a second time.

## Tests-only items

The slice with the highest density of real findings and the lowest risk of a
false positive, so it is where the cleanup starts. A symbol whose only consumer
is its own test suite is not shipping behaviour.
